hol10: 💡 Keeps 4 days refrigerated and freezes well for up to 3 months in individual portions; thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.
💡 Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth before folding it in, otherwise the curds separate in the oven and leave watery pockets. Reheat covered at 700 W for 3 minutes, stirring halfway.
v3: 💡 Keep the cucumber, yogurt and cottage cheese in a separate pot and add them cold; the couscous base keeps 4 days but goes limp with wet dairy sitting on it.
💡 Eat this cold or at room temperature; if you do warm it, 90 seconds at 600 W is plenty, as the roasted chickpeas lose their crunch quickly. Do not freeze, as the couscous turns mushy.
m31: 💡 Pull the chicken at 74°C on the thickest piece and rest it before slicing; even 5 degrees over turns breast dry and stringy after a second heating.
💡 Keeps 4 days chilled. Reheat at 600 W for 2 to 3 minutes with a splash of water over the rice, and add the parsley and lemon squeeze after heating so they stay bright.
m35: 💡 Shrimp tighten and go rubbery when reheated hard, so warm these portions gently at 50 percent power in 60-second bursts until just hot. They keep 3 days in the fridge and are best not frozen once cooked.
💡 Cook the shrimp in two batches so the wok stays searing hot; overcrowding drops the temperature and they boil in their own liquid instead of browning.
m52: 💡 Do not skip the 3-minute rest after air frying; slicing straight away lets the juices run out onto the board, and the chicken will be noticeably drier by day three.
💡 Portions keep 4 days refrigerated and the chicken and rice freeze for up to 2 months. To reheat, air fry at 160°C for 6 to 8 minutes, or microwave at 700 W for 2 to 3 minutes.
m56: 💡 Store the 80 g cottage cheese and paprika separately and spoon it on cold after reheating; microwaved cottage cheese weeps and turns grainy over the rice.
💡 Baby spinach wilts to nothing and goes slimy if stored cooked, so either add it raw when assembling or keep it in the fridge and toss it in while the bowl is still hot.
m44: 💡 Blanching the broccoli for only 3 minutes matters: it finishes cooking in the wok and again on reheating, so anything longer leaves it olive-green and mushy by midweek.
💡 Keeps 4 days refrigerated and freezes for up to 3 months, although the mushrooms and snap peas soften on thawing. Reheat at 700 W for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring once.
m41: 💡 Pull the pork at 63°C and rest it a full 10 minutes; the centre will look faintly pink, which is correct for tenderloin and stops it drying out on reheating.
💡 Keep asparagus, green beans and cherry tomatoes in a separate compartment and reheat only the pork and rice at 50 percent power for 2 minutes, then add the vegetables cold or barely warm.
m24: 💡 Keep the cashews in a small bag and scatter them on after reheating; stored in the sauce they go soft and chalky within a day.
💡 The chicken and sauce keep 4 days in the fridge and freeze well for 3 months without the snow peas, which go grey and limp once frozen. Reheat covered at 700 W for 2 to 3 minutes.
m47: 💡 Mix the cornstarch into cold water until fully dissolved before it goes anywhere near the hot pan, otherwise it seizes into lumps and the glaze never thickens evenly.
💡 The cornstarch glaze thickens further in the fridge, so add a tablespoon of water before microwaving at 700 W for 2 to 3 minutes. Keeps 4 days; freeze the chicken and rice but not the bok choy.
v5: 💡 Take the pan off the heat before stirring the yogurt and cottage cheese in a spoonful at a time; if the sauce is bubbling, the dairy curdles and the masala turns grainy.
💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge but does not freeze well, as the yogurt sauce splits on thawing. Reheat gently at 50 percent power for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring twice, and stop as soon as it is hot.
v7: 💡 Pack the cheddar, Greek yogurt and cottage cheese separately and add them after reheating; heated yogurt goes thin and watery across the rice.
💡 Reheat the rice and sweet potato at 700 W for about 2 minutes, then spoon the bean salsa over cold; it keeps 4 days, but heating it dulls the raw onion, lime and tomato.
m42: 💡 Tilapia is delicate: store the fillets whole in the container, keep only 3 days and do not freeze once cooked, as thawed cooked fish turns watery and falls apart.
💡 Keep the mango salsa in its own pot and spoon it over cold; reheat only the rice and fish, covered, at 50 percent power for 2 minutes so the fish warms through without going rubbery.
bf32: 💡 Congee thickens dramatically as it cools, so stir in 100 ml of broth or water when reheating at 700 W for 3 minutes, and keep the soft-boiled egg, spring onion and ginger in a separate pot.
💡 Pour the egg whites in a thin stream off the heat, stirring in one direction; into boiling congee they clump into rubbery lumps. The base keeps 3 days chilled and freezes for a month.
m74: 💡 Honey glaze burns fast, so baste only in the final 2 to 3 minutes of pan-frying rather than from the start, or the sugars blacken before the chicken reaches 75°C.
💡 Keeps 4 days chilled. Store the crushed cashews and pickled slaw separately, then reheat the chicken, rice and bok choy at 700 W for 2 to 3 minutes and scatter the cashews on last.
m78: 💡 Chicken thighs are forgiving on reheating and stay juicy, so this one reheats well in an air fryer at 180°C for 5 minutes for a fresh char. Keeps 4 days and freezes for 3 months.
💡 Keep the seeds and crispy garlic in a separate small pot; sealed in with the peri peri juices they soften overnight and lose the crunch.
m79: 💡 Coconut rice keeps 4 days chilled and freezes well, but the cabbage slaw should be dressed fresh; stored with lime it weeps and goes limp within hours, so keep it undressed in its own pot.

💡 Pat the marinated thighs dry before searing; the coconut milk marinade steams rather than caramelises if the pan is crowded or the surface is wet. Reheat the chicken and rice at 700 W for 2 to 3 minutes.
